children: has formed a death cross for the first time since June 2023, with its 50-day moving average falling below its 200-day average, according to Barchart.

UPS closed Wednesday at $95.82, with its 50-day and 200-day moving averages converging near the $102-$105 range, according to the accompanying chart. The crossover was marked on the chart alongside a similar setup from June 2023.

The previous death cross was followed by a 22% decline in UPS shares over the next five months, Barchart said. The current chart shows UPS trading below both moving averages after falling from above $110 in July to below $100 in September.
UPS carries a C momentum grade, with its recent performance showing weakness across shorter time frames. The stock's six-month performance was down 1.89% versus a 4.29% gain for the sector median.

Over nine months, UPS was down 4.36%, compared with a 3.88% gain for the sector median. The stock remained up 13.52% over the past year, however, compared with a 5.65% gain for the sector median, representing a 139.35% difference to the sector.

The death cross occurs when a shorter-term moving average falls below a longer-term moving average and is commonly used as a measure of weakening price momentum. UPS's current setup, therefore, comes alongside a sharp deterioration in its shorter-term performance, even as its one-year return remained positive.

title: UPS flashes death cross as momentum weakens
